cases.title: Basic tumor immunologist → population epidemiology of cancer survivorship disparities

evidence.title: TOX-driven epigenetic remodeling locks tumor-infiltrating CD8 T cells into exhaustion in murine melanoma
evidence.text: Exhausted CD8 T cells in solid tumors lose effector function through a stable epigenetic program. Using B16-OVA and MC38 tumors in C57BL/6 mice, we deleted Tox in tumor-specific T cells with CRISPR-Cas9 and profiled 42,000 tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes by single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Tox-deficient cells retained TCF1 and cytotoxic transcripts but failed to persist, revealing that exhaustion is a survival program. Anti-PD-1 treatment expanded the TCF1+ progenitor pool only when Tox was intact. These results define a mechanism that may explain variable patient responses to checkpoint blockade.

evidence.title: Single-cell mapping of the tumor microenvironment during anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse colorectal cancer
evidence.text: We treated MC38 tumor-bearing mice with anti-PD-1 and sampled tumors at four time points for scRNA-seq of 60,000 cells. Myeloid cells expressing Cxcl9 and Cxcl10 clustered near reinvigorated T cells; depleting them with a Csf1r antibody abolished the response. Spatial transcriptomics on tumor sections localized these niches to the tumor margin. The findings identify a myeloid-T cell circuit that could be targeted to improve immunotherapy outcomes for patients.

evidence.title: Metabolic reprogramming of exhausted T cells by mitochondrial pyruvate carrier inhibition
evidence.text: Exhausted T cells show mitochondrial insufficiency. In vitro, inhibiting the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier in chronically stimulated mouse and human T cells restored oxidative metabolism and effector cytokine production. Adoptive transfer of treated OT-I cells into tumor-bearing mice slowed tumor growth. Seahorse assays, flow cytometry and bulk RNA-seq characterized the metabolic switch.

evidence.title: Epigenetic control of T cell exhaustion in solid tumors
evidence.text: This R01 from the NCI Division of Cancer Biology dissects how TOX and NR4A transcription factors establish the exhausted state in tumor-infiltrating T cells. Aim 1 maps chromatin accessibility in mouse tumor models across the exhaustion trajectory. Aim 2 tests whether transient CRISPR perturbation of the TOX locus in adoptively transferred T cells improves control of established tumors. Aim 3 asks whether the same epigenetic marks are present in T cells from resected human melanoma, using banked specimens. The long-term goal is durable immunotherapy for patients whose tumors resist checkpoint blockade.

evidence.title: Personal statement
evidence.text: I am a tumor immunologist whose laboratory studies the molecular mechanisms that silence T cells inside tumors. My group works in mouse models with genetic perturbation, single-cell genomics and adoptive cell transfer, and collaborates with surgical oncology for occasional human tumor specimens. I have led an R01 since 2019 and trained six postdoctoral fellows.

notice.title: Population-Based Research on Cancer Survivorship Disparities (R01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sections.heading: Funding Opportunity Purpose
sections.text: The NCI Division of Cancer Control and Population Sciences invites applications for population-based research on disparities in cancer survivorship outcomes. Studies must use existing population cohorts, cancer registries linked to administrative or claims data, or surveys of survivors to characterize how social determinants of health shape long-term outcomes after a cancer diagnosis.

sections.heading: Research Objectives
sections.text: Responsive applications will examine survivorship outcomes — late effects, second cancers, financial hardship, employment, quality of life, mortality — in populations defined by race, ethnicity, rurality, income or insurance. Applications are expected to use large cohorts or registry linkages with sample sizes adequate for subgroup analysis, and to apply epidemiologic or causal-inference methods. Mixed-methods components with survivor interviews are encouraged.

cases.title: Cardiovascular epidemiologist → cellular mechanisms of cardiomyocyte mitochondrial dysfunction

evidence.title: Cumulative blood pressure exposure and incident heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in a multi-ethnic cohort
evidence.text: In 6,200 participants of a community-based cohort followed for a median of 14 years, we estimated time-weighted cumulative systolic blood pressure from serial visits and modeled incident heart failure with preserved ejection fraction using cause-specific Cox models with inverse-probability weighting for competing death. Each 10 mmHg-year increase was associated with a 1.19-fold hazard, stronger in Black participants. Mediation by left ventricular mass on echocardiography explained a third of the association.
topic_terms: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

evidence.title: Target trial emulation of early statin initiation after myocardial infarction using linked electronic health records
evidence.text: Using EHR data from three health systems linked to state death records, we emulated a target trial of statin initiation within 7 days versus 8–30 days after myocardial infarction among 41,000 adults. With cloning, censoring and weighting, early initiation was associated with lower 1-year mortality. Negative-control outcomes and quantitative bias analysis addressed residual confounding.

evidence.title: Neighborhood deprivation and cardiovascular event rates: a pooled analysis of four US cohorts
evidence.text: We pooled 28,000 participants across four cohorts with geocoded addresses and area-deprivation indices. Multilevel models with cohort random effects estimated event rates for coronary heart disease and stroke. Deprivation was associated with events independent of individual income, with heterogeneity by region.

evidence.title: Life-course cardiovascular risk in diverse populations
evidence.text: This R01 harmonizes exposure histories across five NHLBI cohorts to model how blood pressure, glycemia and lipids accumulate over the life course and translate into heart failure, stroke and coronary events. Methods include g-computation for time-varying exposures, competing-risk models and validation in EHR-based cohorts.

evidence.title: Personal statement
evidence.text: I am a cardiovascular epidemiologist. My research uses longitudinal cohorts and electronic health records to identify determinants of cardiovascular disease and to apply causal-inference methods to observational data. I direct the analytic core of a multi-cohort consortium and have been PI of two R01s.

evidence.title: Randomized trial of early combination therapy versus step-up therapy in newly diagnosed Crohn's disease
evidence.text: Interventional, randomized, open-label, phase III. Principal investigator. 220 adults with newly diagnosed moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease randomized to early anti-TNF plus immunomodulator or conventional step-up care; primary endpoint endoscopic remission at week 52 with serial biomarker sampling.

evidence.title: Serum calprotectin trajectories predict response to vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis: a prospective treatment cohort
evidence.text: We enrolled 180 patients with ulcerative colitis starting vedolizumab at four centers and measured serum and fecal calprotectin at baseline, week 6 and week 14. Group-based trajectory models identified early responders; a trajectory-based rule predicted week-52 clinical remission with an AUC of 0.81. Banked serum was used for proteomic discovery of additional markers.

evidence.title: Ustekinumab versus adalimumab in anti-TNF-naive Crohn's disease: a multicenter randomized trial
evidence.text: In this investigator-initiated trial, 310 patients were randomized to ustekinumab or adalimumab. The primary endpoint, corticosteroid-free clinical remission at week 52, was reached in 61% and 57%. Endoscopic outcomes, safety and patient-reported outcomes are reported. The trial was conducted under an IND with central endoscopy reading.

evidence.title: Biomarker-guided treatment strategies in inflammatory bowel disease
evidence.text: This R01 supports a platform of prospective treatment cohorts and a pragmatic randomized trial comparing biomarker-guided dose intensification with standard care in Crohn's disease. It banks serum, stool and mucosal biopsies from enrolled participants for translational sub-studies with collaborators.

evidence.title: Personal statement

cases.title: Computational statistical geneticist → large-scale human genomic analysis of CKD progression

collaborators.one_line_summary: clinical (clinical observational; runs a chronic kidney disease cohort)

evidence.title: Ancestry-aware polygenic scores from admixed biobank participants improve prediction across populations
evidence.text: Polygenic scores trained in European-ancestry samples lose accuracy in other populations. We developed a method that models local ancestry along the genome and estimates ancestry-specific effect sizes jointly across 480,000 participants of two biobanks. In held-out African- and Hispanic-ancestry samples, prediction of twelve quantitative traits improved by 18–41%. Software is released as an open-source package.

evidence.title: A scalable mixed-model framework for genome-wide association in cohorts with related individuals and longitudinal phenotypes
evidence.text: We present a linear mixed model that handles repeated measurements and cryptic relatedness in biobank-scale data with a randomized trace estimator, reducing run time by an order of magnitude. Applied to serially measured blood pressure in 300,000 participants, the method recovered known loci and identified eleven new ones with trajectory-specific effects.

evidence.title: Fine-mapping causal variants with functional annotations in a multi-ancestry meta-analysis of blood lipids
evidence.text: A consortium meta-analysis of 1.6 million individuals used our annotation-informed fine-mapping approach to resolve credible sets at 900 loci. Colocalization with expression data implicated candidate genes.

evidence.title: Statistical methods for polygenic prediction in diverse populations
evidence.text: This NHGRI R01 develops and validates statistical genetic methods — ancestry-aware polygenic scores, gene-environment interaction tests and Mendelian randomization with pleiotropy — using existing genotyped cohorts and biobanks with linked clinical outcomes. Aim 3 applies the methods to complex disease outcomes recorded in electronic health records.

evidence.title: Personal statement
evidence.text: I am a statistical geneticist. My group develops methods for genome-wide association, polygenic prediction and causal inference in large biobanks and applies them across complex traits; we do not focus on a single disease. Our software is used by several consortia. I hold an NHGRI R01 and an R35.

evidence.title: Interferon-signature-guided anifrolumab in active systemic lupus erythematosus
evidence.text: Interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II. Principal investigator. 140 adults with active SLE stratified by a blood interferon gene signature; primary endpoint SRI-4 response at week 24 with mechanistic sub-studies on serial blood samples.

evidence.title: A randomized phase II trial of B-cell depletion followed by belimumab in lupus nephritis
evidence.text: We randomized 96 patients with active lupus nephritis to rituximab followed by belimumab or rituximab alone across five sites. Complete renal response at week 52 was 52% versus 34%. Serial serum, urine and PBMC samples were banked; B-cell repertoire sequencing showed delayed repopulation of autoreactive clones in the combination arm. The trial was investigator-initiated under an IND held by the first author.

evidence.title: Type I interferon gene signatures predict flare in systemic lupus erythematosus: a prospective biomarker cohort
evidence.text: In 320 patients with SLE followed quarterly for two years, a five-gene interferon score in whole blood predicted flare within 90 days (hazard ratio 2.4). The score was validated in an independent cohort and is now used to stratify enrollment in our trials.

evidence.title: Lupus Clinical Trials Network — biomarker-guided phase II trials
evidence.text: This U01 supports a network of eight sites conducting phase II trials of targeted agents in systemic lupus erythematosus with biomarker-guided enrollment and mechanistic correlative studies. The PI chairs the protocol committee and leads the interferon-signature stratification strategy.

evidence.title: Personal statement
evidence.text: I am a rheumatologist and clinical trialist. I have been principal investigator of four interventional trials in systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, including two investigator-initiated phase II trials under my own IND, and I lead the biomarker strategy of a multi-site trials network. My K23 and R01 built a prospective SLE cohort with a biospecimen repository.

cases.title: Basic human immunologist → mechanistic immunology, Basic Experimental Studies with Humans Required

collaborators.one_line_summary: clinical (clinical trials; runs CAR-T trials in lymphoma)

evidence.title: CRISPR screens in primary human T cells identify regulators of TCR signal strength
evidence.text: We performed genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in primary CD4 and CD8 T cells from twelve healthy blood donors, reading out phospho-ERK and CD69 by flow cytometry after TCR stimulation. Hits were validated by arrayed knockout and phospho-flow across donors, and single-cell RNA-seq of edited cells mapped the transcriptional consequences. Donor-to-donor variation in hit strength tracked with HLA genotype. No animals were used.

evidence.title: Interleukin-2 receptor tuning in human regulatory T cells isolated from patient blood
evidence.text: Regulatory T cells from the blood of 30 patients with autoimmune disease and 20 healthy donors were sorted and edited to titrate IL2RA expression. Phospho-STAT5 responses and suppressive function in co-culture defined a receptor-density threshold for stable FOXP3 expression. Bulk ATAC-seq profiled the edited cells.

evidence.title: A human tonsil organoid system reveals germinal center B cell selection rules
evidence.text: Tonsil tissue from surgical specimens was dissociated and reaggregated into organoids that support germinal center reactions ex vivo. Perturbing T follicular helper signals with blocking antibodies and CRISPR editing altered B cell selection, read out by single-cell BCR sequencing.

evidence.title: Mechanisms of T cell receptor signal integration in human T cells
evidence.text: This R01 uses primary human T cells from healthy donors and patient blood, genome editing, phospho-flow and single-cell genomics to define how signal strength is set and tuned. Aim 3 tests candidate regulators in T cells from patients on checkpoint blockade, using blood collected under an existing IRB protocol.

evidence.title: Personal statement
evidence.text: I am a basic human immunologist. My laboratory studies T cell receptor signaling in primary human cells from healthy donors and patients using CRISPR perturbation, phospho-flow cytometry and single-cell genomics; we do no animal work. I have never led a clinical trial, but two of my closest collaborators run CAR-T trials and I lead correlative science for one of them.

cases.title: Health services researcher → mechanisms of beta-cell dysfunction

collaborators.one_line_summary: health_systems (implementation science; hybrid trials in primary care)

evidence.title: Racial and ethnic disparities in continuous glucose monitor use among Medicaid enrollees with type 2 diabetes: a claims analysis
evidence.text: Using claims for 410,000 adult Medicaid enrollees with type 2 diabetes across eleven states, we measured continuous glucose monitor uptake after coverage expansion. Multivariable models adjusted for insulin use, comorbidity and county supply of endocrinologists. Uptake among Black and Hispanic enrollees lagged White enrollees by 40%, with wide variation by state policy. Difference-in-differences estimates linked prior-authorization removal to a 9-point increase in uptake.

evidence.title: Quality of diabetes care in federally qualified health centers: a retrospective EHR cohort of 120 clinics
evidence.text: We assembled a retrospective cohort of 260,000 patients with diabetes from the electronic health records of 120 federally qualified health centers and measured guideline-concordant care (HbA1c testing, statin prescribing, eye and foot exams) from 2018 to 2023. Hierarchical models attributed variation to clinic-level staffing and telehealth adoption. Utilization outcomes included emergency visits and hospitalizations.

evidence.title: A hybrid type 2 effectiveness-implementation study of community health worker support for diabetes self-management in safety-net clinics
evidence.text: In eight safety-net clinics, a community health worker program was rolled out in a stepped-wedge design. Effectiveness outcomes were HbA1c and appointment adherence; implementation outcomes were reach, adoption and fidelity assessed with the RE-AIM framework and staff interviews. As co-investigator, the health services team led the EHR-based outcome ascertainment and cost analysis.

evidence.title: Policy levers and disparities in diabetes technology access
evidence.text: This R01 links Medicaid and Medicare claims with state policy databases to estimate how coverage rules, prior authorization and provider supply shape access to diabetes technologies, and simulates the effects of policy alternatives on disparities in utilization and outcomes.

evidence.title: Personal statement
evidence.text: I am a health services researcher studying diabetes care quality, utilization and disparities with claims and electronic health record data. I have served as co-investigator on one hybrid effectiveness-implementation study and lead an R01 on policy and diabetes technology access. I have no laboratory training and do not conduct clinical or bench research.
